Senator Robin Padilla on Wednesday reacted to the remarks of Senator Erwin Tulfo, who said he was hurt by the reports that three fellow senators supposedly voted against dismissing a petition seeking to unseat him.
“Gano’n ba? Wala naman dapat ikatampo siguro. Baka hindi pa lang niya alam kung ano ‘yung totoo,” Padilla said in an ambush interview.
(Is that so? I don't think there's any reason to be upset. Maybe he just doesn't know the truth yet.)

Padilla was said to be among the three Senate Electoral Tribunal (SET) members who reportedly voted against dismissing a motion for reconsideration on the ruling that junked the petition to remove Tulfo from office over alleged citizenship issues, among other grounds.
Tulfo said he was a bit hurt by the reports, believing he was on good terms with two of the three senators who supposedly betrayed him.

He also posted a cartoon on his official Facebook page depicting three individuals preparing to stab him in the back. The arms holding the knives bore the names “Sen. Padilla,” “Sen. Villar” and “Sen. Pia.”

The SET is composed of three Supreme Court justices and six senators. Senators Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan, Bam Aquino, and Lito Lapid represent the majority bloc, while Senators Pia Cayetano, Robin Padilla, and Camille Villar represent the minority. — RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: Australian MP Helen Haines loses both legs after car attack as suspect appears in court
articles.summary: Doctors have amputated both of Helen Haines legs after the Australian lawmaker was hit in an apparent deliberate attack. The suspected driver involved in the attack has appeared in court.

image.caption: The attack on Helen Haines has shocked Australia and brought up questions of security for lawmakersImage: Martin Keep/AFP

blocks.text: Helen Haines, an Australian lawmaker struck by a car in an apparently deliberate attack on Monday, has lost both of her legs, her husband said on Wednesday.
Counterterrorism investigators have joined a police probe into the incident, which occurred outside Haines' constituency office in Wangaratta, northeast of the Victorian capital, Melbourne.

A 43-year-old suspect, Brendan N. from nearby Tarrawingee, appeared in Wangaratta Magistrates' Court on Wednesday charged with intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury and causing harm to a federal official.
Haines loses both legs after apparent attack

The independent MP underwent surgery on Monday night after suffering what were described as critical injuries in the incident, with national broadcaster ABC and the daily Sydney Morning Herald reporting on Tuesday that her left leg had been amputated.
Doctors then proceeded to amputate her right leg on Wednesday after having tried to save it.
"The good news in all this is that Helen is alive and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family," Phil Haines told reporters in Melbourne.
"We are grateful and thankful that at this stage, both her heart and her mind are in good shape," he said.
What do we know about the suspected attack on Haines?
Haines, 65, was hit by an SUV, which police said was a white Toyota, outside her office. She suffered serious injuries, particularly to her lower body.

ABC cited witnesses as saying they heard a bang and then saw a woman pinned between two cars. Later reports from witnesses said that after first pinning Haines against her own car, the driver reversed and rammed into her a second time.
The driver was arrested shortly after, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
Albanese said early investigations suggested the driver made a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading items at the trunk of her car.
"This wasn't an accident. There was a deliberate act, it would appear," he told ABC.

The suspect's lawyer, Chirag Patel, told Magistrate Allison Vaughan on Wednesday that his client suffers from a rare neurological condition, as well as an undiagnosed mental health condition. He also said the defendant was suffering from a concussion.
Local barber ran to assist
Local barber Ricky Jeffries, whose shop is next to Haines' office, has been widely hailed as a hero after he ran to pull the driver out of the car and restrained him until police arrived.

blocks.caption: Barber Ricky Jefferies has been called a hero for restraining the driverImage: Seven Network/REUTERS

blocks.text: Jeffries downplayed his role, despite having intervened in what could have been a highly dangerous situation, as the man had a knife in the car.
"He [the driver] did have a knife. He didn't ​pull it ‌out. I just wasn't comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away," he said.
Jefferies said he then held the man down until ‌police arrived.
"I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and ‌he was ​no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can't leave," he said.
Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: "My wife would be disappointed if I'm injured."
"The other people here were just, they did so much more than me ... they deserve the credit," he added.
Political violence on the rise: PM Albanese
Albanese said it was too early to speculate about the possible motive behind the suspected attack, but pointed to rising political violence.
"The temperature has increased in recent times," Albanese added, "I've expressed that concern to people in the media."

blocks.caption: Prime Minister Albanese has said the incident seemed 'no accident'Image: Marek Ladzinski/ZUMA/picture alliance

blocks.text: Ben Carroll, the state premier for Victoria where Wangaratta is located, said he was "appalled" by the attack, adding: "I know how devastating this will be for the Wangaratta community and all those who Helen represents."
At a separate press conference, Albanese said everyone was "praying for her full recovery."

Although it has not yet been established whether the incident was deliberate, there has been an increase in threats and harassment targeting lawmakers and other senior public officials in Australia and elsewhere in recent years.
Haines had worked as a nurse and a midwife before entering parliament in 2019. She is known for her stance on stronger climate action.

articles.title: More than 1.5 million Canadian Crime Stoppers tips leaked, CBC exclusive finds

image.caption: Andrew Rivard is one of tens of thousands of Canadian tipsters whose personal information was exposed in the Crime Stoppers hack. (Tyson Koschik/CBC)

blocks.text: When Andrew Rivard spotted a Crime Stoppers ad offering a $2,000 reward for tips in the winter of 2025, he decided to report what he knew about illegal cigarette sales in his neighbourhood.
Rivard’s original tip shows he disclosed his full name. He says he trusted the organization’s long-standing promise to protect the identities of all tipsters.
"I was told nothing would come of it; no one would come to me with, you know, I guess, resentment," Rivard said. "I just was hoping it would be that exactly — anonymous."

But the Manitoba man's report — along with information from more than 1.5 million other tips submitted to Canadian Crime Stoppers programs over the last 25 years — was exposed in a massive data breach, an exclusive CBC investigation has found.
The personal information captured in some compromised tips was detailed enough for CBC to contact more than a dozen tipsters — including Rivard — who reacted with shock and fear for their safety.
"It’s very scary, to be honest," said Rivard, who now worries his home address and phone number may be used by criminals for retaliation.
Rivard’s original tip as it appeared in the leaked data, including his full name. CBC retroactively redacted other personally identifiable information. (Valérie Ouellet/CBC)

The data was stolen last March by hacktivist collective Internet Yiff Machine. In a manifesto, the group said it wanted to disprove the claim by P3 Global Intel — the company hired by Crime Stoppers to manage its tips — that the platform was "anonymous" and "secure."

A copy of the hacked data was made available to researchers and journalists, including CBC, by Distributed Denial of Secrets, a U.S. non-profit that archives and publishes hacked and leaked documents it deems to be in the public interest.

CBC took extensive precautions to protect this sensitive data throughout its investigation. Our security measures included, but were not limited to, encryption and working in a self-contained, offline environment. The sensitive information was only accessible to a small number of CBC journalists working on the project. Ultimately, CBC intends to destroy its copy of the dataset.

Beyond confirming they were hacked over six months ago, the Canadian Crime Stoppers Association (CCSA) and individual chapters have not spoken about the extent of the breach, only saying they await a detailed report from Navigate360, the company that owns the P3 platform.
This is the first time precise figures on how many Canadian tipsters were compromised in the breach — and the severity of the information exposed — have been made public.

items: Canadian investigation launched into data breach that exposed millions of IDs
Hacker took 100,000 documents in 2025 'cyber incident,' Kingston Police say

blocks.text: Our interviews and analysis of Canadian content in the leaked data suggest that Crime Stoppers, along with the company it contracted to manage its database, failed to protect tipsters' identities, left personal information unredacted and improperly retained decades of sensitive records.

"For a system that has been designed to promise anonymity to the users, that has failed categorically," said Prof. Ali Dehghantanha, the Canada Research Chair in Cybersecurity and Threat Intelligence at the University of Guelph.
He’s one of two experts who were shown our methodology and limited samples of the data from a secure CBC laptop.

After seeing CBC’s main findings, the RCMP shared concerns that the breach could “jeopardize public safety, including the safety of tipsters, individuals identified in tips and police officers," it said in a statement, adding it was originally told the leak did not include Canadian data or personal information.
CBC also shared the same information with the CCSA, which declined an interview.

In a written statement, the organization’s president, David J. Forster, said they “recognize the concern and uncertainty this incident has created, particularly for people who trust Crime Stoppers with sensitive information.”
There are currently 68 Crime Stoppers chapters registered as non-profits in Canada, according to data from the Canada Revenue Agency.
Professor Ali Dehghantanha is one of two cybersecurity experts who examined samples of the data. (Li Yanjun/CBC)
Tips about high-profile Canadian investigations

Crime Stoppers is a network of civilian-run non-profits that collects anonymous tips on crime and suspicious activity. It operates independently of law enforcement, though it refers a portion of tips back to them to assist in investigations.

The organization often appeals to the public, in partnership with police, for help with unsolved crimes and to advance investigations — all with the promise of anonymity for tipsters who contact them.

CBC’s analysis of Canadian tips found mentions of many high-profile cases that generated significant public attention — from Barry and Honey Sherman’s murders to Amber Tuccaro's disappearance, Montreal’s Luka Magnotta case and, more recently, the international manhunt for Ryan Wedding.

items: To see our methodology, scroll to the bottom of this story or click here.

blocks.text: Many of the tips dealt with serious allegations, with some people explicitly saying they feared retribution for speaking out.
Citizens called with information about alleged murderers, terrorists and pedophiles or incriminating details about people they were close to, like family members on the run or breaching court orders.

In 2012, police asked for the public’s help in identifying the voice of a man with a connection to missing Indigenous woman Amber Tuccaro. CBC found hundreds of tips mentioning her disappearance in the leaked Crime Stoppers tips. (Valérie Ouellet/CBC)

A third of all tips talked about drugs and drug trafficking; hundreds reported suspicious activity in their neighbourhoods, often naming individuals and implicating organized crime, biker gangs or drug cartels — including the Hells Angels, Rock Machine and Outlaws, as well as B.C.’s Red Scorpions and Independent Soldiers.

items: 'Surrey Six' murders mastermind Jamie Bacon released from prison

blocks.text: Notes in the data from Crime Stoppers staff suggest some of those tips led to real-life consequences: Nearly 49,000 tips were linked to a case cleared by an arrest or criminal charges, while nearly 1,000 tipsters were approved for cash rewards.
"I am concerned. I am really worried," said Dehghantanha, who has conducted digital forensics investigations for over a decade.
“I am really concerned about these records … being in the hands of the wrong people, while those people who have been impacted are not aware of that and do not have any support.”
Over a million Canadian tips leaked from Crime Stoppers database
That's exactly the situation one Canadian woman is facing. CBC agreed to withhold her identity given her safety concerns.
She gave a tip about the murder of a loved one, which was unsolved at the time.
"I just feel all the anxiety and scared feeling come back," said the woman. Police have now charged an individual with murder.
"They were capable of hurting my loved one. They could come back and hurt one of us."
Tipsters self-identified in over 4,300 tips, data suggests

More than 850,000 tips — about half of all Canadian records identified by CBC — included personally identifiable information about tipsters, individuals named in allegations and even Crime Stoppers staff and police.

Street addresses and phone numbers appeared most frequently, alongside tens of thousands of personal emails, licence plates and hundreds of banking details related to cash rewards — information that could all be used to uncover an individual's identity.
We could not determine in every instance whether the information belonged to a tipster, a victim or those accused of a crime.

However, CBC found that in over 4,300 reports, tipsters introduced themselves with a full name, although Crime Stoppers explicitly tells the public to avoid including identifying details. Still, this represented a fraction of reports, at less than one per cent of all entries over 25 years. CBC wasn't able to verify whether all names were legitimate.
In 2021, police sought the public's help in identifying a suspect caught on video near the home of billionaire philanthropists Barry and Honey Sherman. (Evan Mitsui/CBC)
Despite hundreds of those tips containing clear staff warnings that a tipster had "self-identified" or had been "exposed," the information still appeared in the database unredacted.
Storing all these data points together is a gold mine for fraudsters, said Dehghantanha.
"Imagine I am calling you and talking about the tip that you have provided and asking for more information. Immediately, I build ... trust," he said.

items: Shock and surprise after FBI arrests Canadian cybersecurity expert in ShinyHunters hacking case

blocks.text: A name or phone number on a list might not seem like much, but it’s enough to do serious damage, said Ben Coon, chief intelligence officer of U.S. cybersecurity firm Unit 221B, who was also shown limited samples of the data.

"From what I saw, there's so much low-hanging fruit here that we could ask questions," said Coon, who said the data could be used for crimes ranging from financial fraud and extortion to money laundering.
Beyond what was collected, experts say the decision to store decades of historical tips in a single place defies basic data retention standards.
"If a tip is closed, does that need to stay online?" said Coon. "The answer to that, to me, is no."
Both experts agree that even though Crime Stoppers uses a third party to manage its data, it is still responsible for auditing how well it is secured.
"You can always outsource the operation … [and] the work," said Dehghantanha. "But you cannot outsource the accountability. You are always accountable when you are collecting the data."
Hacker claims data not publicly available online

Both cybersecurity experts said they were surprised CBC had found the data as they couldn’t locate copies of it online, which they said was reassuring. But they added that once a dataset has been leaked, it’s generally available somewhere.

In an email exchange with CBC News in September, someone purporting to represent Internet Yiff Machine wrote, "I briefly attempted to sell it publicly; however, changed my mind and no copy has made it into the public yet."
They added that the security measures of P3, which was storing Crime Stoppers' tips, were "terrible" and that the platform is still vulnerable.
"I wouldn’t trust [the hackers] at all," said Dehghantanha. "Selling [data] on the underground market is not that difficult, right…. There is a demand."
Internet Yiff Machine’s manifesto includes lines critical of police departments and for-profit prisons. (Valérie Ouellet/CBC)

In a statement, the Canadian Crime Stoppers Association said, "If there is information within the leaked records that could identify people who submitted tips, it is an extremely serious issue." It added that protecting people's safety and anonymity is its "highest priority."

It did not directly comment on the precise figures shared by CBC, but said that it has been communicating with the third-party platform "to assess what records may have been affected, what personal information may have been exposed and what measures were taken to enhance the security of the platform."

"With regard to notifying individuals identified in the records, CCSA has concerns about doing so without jeopardizing the anonymity and safety of tipsters," it said, adding that "the information available to us does not distinguish people who submitted tips from people identified in them."
"We will share further verified information as it becomes available, while ensuring that our communications do not create additional risks for individuals."

Navigate360, the U.S.-based company that owns the P3 platform, did not respond to CBC's requests for comment, which included questions about what security measures it had taken since the hack, whether it had shared reports with Crime Stoppers about the compromised data and whether it was still collecting tips.

items: ShinyHunters hackers say they breached FBI, stole employee data
RCMP warn of new scam involving the purchase of gold

blocks.text: The RCMP told CBC that at the time of the leak, it was “advised that Canadian data had not been affected based on the results of the preliminary personally identifiable information (PII) assessment."
"Then, in May 2026, the RCMP was informed by Crime Stoppers that the data breach did include Canadian data but would not contain PII of persons who have reported.”
The national police service added that it is now “engaged with the Canadian Crime Stoppers Association to determine the full scope of the incident."

It stated that it has not received reports of anyone being threatened as a result of the breach and advised anyone with concerns about their submitted information to contact the organization or their local chapter.

The Toronto Police Service, which uses tips from Toronto Crime Stoppers — the chapter with the most tips in the leak — told CBC that the group had notified it of a hack in March, but that it "has not received any information indicating the safety of officers, tipsters or members of the public has been compromised."
As for Rivard, the Manitoba man whose tip was exposed in the leak, he says Crime Stoppers should have been more transparent.
"It might have been embarrassing, but own up to it, just tell the public, let them know, and they might have your trust after, they might not: Let them decide."
Methodology: How CBC identified Canadian tips in the Crime Stoppers hack

This investigation is based on CBC’s analysis of more than 8.3 million raw records leaked in March 2026. The breached data originated from P3 Global Intel, a U.S.-based tip management software owned by the company Navigate360. A copy of this hacked data was released to journalists, including CBC, by Distributed Denial of Secrets, a non-profit whistleblower site that publishes hacked documents it deems to be in the public interest. The data contains unverified criminal allegations that have not necessarily been investigated by police or proven in court.
CBC considered a tip to be Canadian if it was submitted to a Canadian Crime Stoppers chapter or contained specific Canadian geographic and linguistic references.

We identified a grand total of 1.6 million records using these combined methodologies. The vast majority were tips submitted directly to Canadian Crime Stoppers chapters (97.98%). The remaining 32,000 tips (2.02%) were submitted to U.S. and international Crime Stoppers chapters, but they all contained Canadian references, such as city names, postal codes, phone area codes or the names of government institutions.
The data was compared against a list compiled by our team of over 700 crime-related keywords, including the names of victims, suspects, missing persons and high-profile police operations.

For this analysis, CBC defined personal identifying information (PII) as: a tipster’s full name, any complete street address, postal code, direct phone number, personal email, vehicle licence plate, personal social media account and/or banking details. Publicly advertised phone numbers of Crime Stoppers chapters and police departments, as well as general switchboards, tiplines, hotlines, general emails and the physical addresses of chapters and police departments were excluded from our PII analysis.

We used Google’s Gemini AI to help us draft, troubleshoot and optimize computer programming scripts in Python and SQLite to structure and systemically analyze a dataset too massive to process manually, (e.g. with spreadsheets). Every suggestion, piece of logic, and code generated by Gemini was independently reviewed by our data journalist to ensure integrity and adherence to CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices. All data outputs were rigorously audited in the same way. The interface was strictly used to generate computer code and was not permitted to make autonomous decisions, run the code itself or access the source database at any time.

CBC/Radio-Canada's corporate agreement with Gemini stipulates that our data is kept strictly private. None of our prompts, uploaded files or chats can be used to improve Google's AI models, and no human reviewers can access our conversations.
Methodology, coding and data analysis by Valérie OuelletData analysis and additional research by Michelle Allan

articles.title: More than 16 years after BP's Deepwater Horizon disaster, marine life has not recovered
articles.summary: 16 years after one of the deadliest oil spills in history — BP's Deepwater Horizon — there is measurable evidence that wildlife is in serious decline and not recovering in the Gulf of Mexico where…

image.caption: On April 21, 2010, a deadly explosion on the offshore oil rig Deepwater Horizon had crews battling for hours, and the resulting oil spill lasted for months. (Reuters/U.S. Coast Guard/Handout)

blocks.text: Climate·New

16 years after one of the deadliest oil spills in history — BP's Deepwater Horizon — there is measurable evidence that wildlife is in serious decline and not recovering in the Gulf of Mexico where the disaster occurred. Through trawling, sound waves and DNA analysis, researchers showed persistent declines of around 60 per cent in some species in the years since.
Fishes, crustaceans, squid show persistent declines and even chemical compounds in their tissues
More than 16 years after one of the deadliest oil spills in history, a highly comprehensive study has found that life in the waters of the Gulf of Mexico remains severely in decline.

The Deepwater Horizon oil rig, operated by BP off the coast of Louisiana, exploded on April 20, 2010 — killing 11 people and injuring 17 others. During the three months that followed, as much as 4.9 million barrels of oil gushed into the Gulf, according to a U.S. government task force. The environmental catastrophe had a devastating impact on marine life, which continues today.

"A lot of things died right off the bat," said Tracey Sutton, a biological oceanographer at the Guy Harvey Oceanographic Research Center of NOVA Southeastern University whose team has been studying the impacts of the spill for years.

Their research found that some species declined by 60 to 85 per cent in the immediate three and a half years after the spill. Sutton's latest report, combining another eight years of detailed scanning and sampling, was just published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Time hasn't helped the situation, according to the authors.

"That low state has just maintained low," Sutton said, explaining that the dense patches of prey that predators need are missing, resulting in a "decline in things like deep-diving whales and dolphins" as well as fishes, shrimps and squids.
The immediate aftermath of the Deepwater Horizon spill killed lots of marine life, and the authors of a new study say that decline has persisted. (Charlie Riedel/The Associated Press)
Lingering in the deep
The most likely cause of this decline, the study suggests, is the Deepwater Horizon disaster, not least of which because their sampling is still finding remnants of all that spilled oil.
"What we've seen is the persistence of some of the worst components in the oil … polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, or PAHs. That's the really bad stuff," Sutton told CBC News.

The study found these oil-derived compounds inside the muscle tissue and eggs of deep-sea fishes and squid, potentially affecting health and reproduction. The authors also suggest these lingering PAHs can affect some male fishes' sense of smell, which they use to find mates.
Deepsea experts who weren't involved with the research say the study accounted for the natural factors that might affect fish abundance, such as temperature, availability of food and oxygen.

"They eliminate any other factors," said Fabio De Leo, senior scientist at Ocean Networks Canada and a professor at the University of Victoria. "And so the probable cause here is the 87 days of gushing oil through the Gulf for Mexico."
Parsing out environmental factors is a sign of the report's strength, says Kelly Robinson, an associate professor at the School of Biological Sciences at the University of Louisiana at Lafayette.
"Sometimes when you work on data, it can show you a different side," said Robinson. "But if it keeps showing you the same message, that's probably what's happening.”
More than a decade later, researchers say chemical compounds from the oil spill have made their way into fish tissue. (Rich Matthews/The Associated Press)
Diverse and essential
Experts say that the negative effect on species has a larger effect for the whole Gulf ecosystem and its role in helping capture carbon in its depths.

The deep pelagic zone, where Sutton and his team surveyed sampled fishes, crustaceans and cephalopods (such as squid) for years, is an umbrella term for a range of depths — anywhere from around 200 metres to 1,500 metres below the surface.

While sunlight stops relatively high up in that zone, the biodiversity doesn't. Lanternfish, stingrays, sperm whales, krill and many more aquatic species are all normally found throughout these depths and regularly migrate between them.

items: Deepwater Horizon site still mostly bereft of life — except for parasite-covered crabs

blocks.text: "You have to remember that these animals feed at the surface," De Leo said. “They migrate downwards and then they respire at that [level]. So the carbon dioxide gets dissolved into the water and there are nutrients that they regenerate back into the water."

"They are a train that's moving energy from the surface to the deep very efficiently," Robinson adds. "And so if we see a decline in that, it's like taking cars away from a train, right? All of a sudden you're not moving as much material."

These species effectively act as a "biological pump" for carbon, and it's one of the ways that oceans help absorb carbon dioxide from the surface, including the excess greenhouse gases humans are pumping into the atmosphere. The waters still dissolve CO2 on their own, but this study shows how pollution can weaken this service that the oceans provide.
Oil booms like this were deployed to try and contain the oil spill, but the volume proved too much and many failed. (Carlos Barria/Reuters)
Risk of future offshore drilling
The Trump administration's promise to "drill, baby, drill" has led to a push for the U.S. to extract more oil and natural gas, including new areas of offshore oil exploration.

In Canada, economic uncertainty has led to the Carney government's support for Pacific Link, a proposed oil pipeline from Alberta to B.C's coast, destined for overseas markets. Despite promised ocean protections, experts fear a long-lasting impact if an oil tanker were to be damaged and leak.
"There's more discussion about increasing oil transport in these areas of the Pacific," De Leo told CBC News from Victoria.
"We're unlikely to have something of [Deepwater Horizon’s] magnitude but there's potentially more risk if there's more traffic," De Leo said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Anand Ram is a reporter and producer with CBC's science and climate unit. He's worked as a reporter covering technology, business and the environment and as a producer with The National.

articles.title: Carney’s Turkish balancing act must include business, defence and human rights
articles.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney heads to Turkey, seeking closer trade, energy and defence ties with a strategically important NATO ally. The historic visit marks a turnaround in relations once soured by a…

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan walk to the prime minister's car following a meeting in Ankara, Turkey, on July 7. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

Prime Minister Mark Carney heads to Turkey, seeking closer trade, energy and defence ties with a strategically important NATO ally. The historic visit marks a turnaround in relations once soured by a Canadian arms embargo. But Ankara’s crackdown on dissent tests Carney’s promise to balance economic pragmatism with Canadian values.
Carney visits Turkey, courting a powerful NATO ally despite fresh concerns about human rights

Prime Minister Mark Carney departs for Turkey on Wednesday for a three-day visit with a strategically important NATO ally whose economic and defence industries have become increasingly attractive to Ottawa.
The trip includes meetings with President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan in Ankara and business leaders in Istanbul, and is the first dedicated bilateral visit to Turkey by a Canadian prime minister.
The meetings are a sign of warming relations between the two countries after Canada imposed a de facto arms embargo for several years.

Ottawa initially froze and then cancelled military permits in 2021 over allegations Ankara had redirected Canadian-manufactured drone parts to Azerbaijani forces during the conflict with Armenia over the disputed region of Nagorno-Karabakh. The policy has since been eased.

The visit also comes a month after Turkish authorities launched a sweeping and unprecedented nationwide crackdown on dissent and civil society, heavily focusing on the systematic dismantling of LGBTQ+ and HIV-advocacy organizations.
His friends were arrested in Turkey’s 2SLGBTQ+ crackdown
Senior federal officials, speaking on background ahead of the trip, said the visit is in keeping with the prime minister's foreign policy.
"Canada is meeting this moment with values based realism. We are pursuing an approach that is both principled and pragmatic," said one official at a technical briefing.
"Principled in its commitment to the fundamental values of freedom, human rights, sustainability and solidarity. Pragmatic in recognizing that not every partner will share all of those values."

items: Turkey's president gifted Carney a revolver at NATO summit. Carney gave him maple syrup
No longer taboo, Canada's defence industry steps into Europe's spotlight

blocks.text: Three issues are likely to dominate Carney's visit: negotiating a free trade agreement, expanding co-operation in energy and strategic industries and developing a closer defence-industrial relationship.
Canada does about $4.3 billion in trade with Turkey. Carney and Erdoğan formally announced the launch of free trade negotiations during the NATO summit in Ankara on July 7.

Carney is attempting to build a stronger strategic partnership with Turkey at a time when Canada is seeking to diversify its international economic relationships and reduce its dependence on the United States.
The prime minister will be accompanied by Foreign Minister Anita Anand and Energy Minister Tim Hodgeson.
Canada pitching Turkey on Candu reactors
Turkey is expanding its nuclear-energy industry as part of a broader strategy to diversify electricity generation and reduce dependence on imported fossil fuels.
Canada sees a possible commercial opportunity for its Candu nuclear reactor technology.
In June, the Canadian and Turkish trade ministers explicitly identified potential co-operation involving Candu reactors.

This is significant because nuclear projects involve enormous long-term commitments, including financing, fuel arrangements, technology transfers, regulatory co-operation and industrial participation.
Federal officials were asked whether a deal was possible during the trip and said they were "not in a position to say anything about any specific outcomes at this point."
There could be more progress on the defence industrial side of the relationship.

items: Ottawa plans Crown corporation to break defence procurement logjam
Canada's next defence fight won’t be over spending. It’ll be over trust

blocks.text: Canada's Secretary of State for Defence Procurement, Stephen Fuhr, visited the country in May 2026, described Turkey as a trusted partner and framed the burgeoning relationship in terms of Carney's push for closer co-operation among middle powers.
"Individually we're just not big enough, but collectively we are," Fuhr said.
In a recent interview with Defense News, Fuhr identified ammunition production, drones and counter-drone systems as key areas for potential co-operation with Turkey.

He also suggested that future collaboration could involve co-development programmes rather than simple off-the-shelf purchases, particularly in sectors where Canada is seeking faster capability growth without having to start from scratch.
Carney and Erdoğan speak as the prime minister leaves a bilateral meeting in Ankara in July. (Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press)

The dispute over military exports is rarely — if ever — mentioned between the two countries and senior federal officials said Tuesday that Canada continues to apply its export-control framework, including assessments of the risk that Canadian military equipment could contribute to violations of international humanitarian law or be transferred to unauthorized users.

"We are looking at each potential export on a case by case basis and that is the Minister of Foreign Affairs who reviews all of those, but this is a growing partnership and it's an important one," said one official.

"The resumption of more regular contact with Turkey has enabled us to have exactly these kinds of conversations. We are in a position to resume a more regular export relationship and we will continue to monitor."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Murray Brewster is the senior defence writer for CBC News, based in Ottawa. He has covered the Canadian military and foreign policy from Parliament Hill for over a decade. Among other assignments, he spent a total of 15 months on the ground covering the Afghan war for The Canadian Press. Prior to that, he covered defence issues and politics for CP in Nova Scotia for 11 years and was bureau chief for Standard Broadcast News in Ottawa.

articles.title: Canadian housing market 'on its knees' as odds of Bank of Canada rate hike rise
articles.summary: The Bank of Canada has not raised interest rates since July 2023. And while an eighth-consecutive hold is widely-predicted next week, a growing number of economists and traders are now expecting the…

image.caption: Experts say a rate hike from the Bank of Canada on Oct. 28 would have significant impacts on the country's battered real estate market. (Michel Aspirot/CBC/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Business·New

The Bank of Canada has not raised interest rates since July 2023. And while an eighth-consecutive hold is widely-predicted next week, a growing number of economists and traders are now expecting the central bank to hike its trend-setting rate to tamp down stubborn inflation.
A rate hike in October would have significant impacts on Canada's battered real estate market, experts say
The Bank of Canada has not raised interest rates since July 2023.

And while an eighth-consecutive hold is widely-predicted next week, a growing number of economists and traders are now expecting the central bank to hike its trend-setting rate to tamp down stubborn inflation.

Mortgage and debt experts say higher rates would have significant impacts on Canada's sagging real estate market. Payments on variable-rate mortgages would rise immediately, along with rates for new fixed mortgages. The pool of eligible buyers would shrink, shifting power from sellers to those who can qualify for the financing needed to make a purchase. Home prices could dip lower.

"The housing market is kind of on its knees right now, and rising rates is like tossing a drowning guy an anchor," said Scott Terrio, manager of consumer insolvency at Ontario-based Hoyes Michalos & Associates.
He says a hike "would reverberate massively."
Could an interest rate hike see home prices fall?
The volume of home sales nationwide is currently at a 25-year low, says Ben Rabidoux of Ontario-based Edge Realty Analytics.
He describes confidence among buyers today as "unbelievably weak across the country," owing to a slew of economic uncertainties ranging from the Canada-U.S. trade war to the impact of AI on jobs.
"The reality is that when we look at per capita home sales, we're already back to 1990s levels, which [was] a really terrible recessionary environment."
On home prices, Rabidoux believes "a gradual grind lower over the next three or six months is very plausible" if interest rates start rising.
That perfect Ontario real estate listing might be staged by AI. Here's what to watch for
Last week, the Canadian Real Estate Association downgraded its forecast for 2026 home sales activity for a third straight quarter.
The industry group referenced a "notably more hawkish tone from the Bank of Canada," as it called for 444,530 homes to be sold by year-end, a 5.2 per cent drop from 2025.
The Bank of Canada's policy rate has stood still at 2.25 per cent since a quarter-point cut in October 2025.

Governor Tiff Macklem has recently warned the bank may need to raise borrowing costs if energy prices remain elevated. On Saturday, he said there is "no resolution in sight for the conflict in the Middle East" that has roiled global energy markets for the past several months.

items: CREA revises down 2026 home sales forecast again as September transactions fall 7.7% over same month last year
Inflation rises to 3.1% in September, as fuel prices push higher: StatsCan

blocks.text: On Monday, the latest inflation data from Statistics Canada put a spotlight on soaring energy costs. The report showed rising fuel prices have yet to meaningfully spill into other sectors of the economy. However, the Bank of Canada's latest survey, also released on Monday, found businesses are bracing for higher prices.
Odds of rate hike 'not a slam dunk'

The consensus in a recent Bloomberg survey still points to a hold, but so far this week, the Bank of Montreal, RBC Dominion Securities and Desjardins Group have flipped their predictions for Oct. 28 from a hold to a hike.

According to Bloomberg data, traders in the overnight swap market now put the odds of a 25-basis point rate hike from the Bank of Canada next week at 87 per cent, up from 70 per cent earlier this week. Swap market data measures the gap between today's interest rate and the future rate traders are betting on.
Canada's economy still resilient, but U.S. trade war taking its toll
Derek Holt, head of capital markets economics at Scotiabank, is among those calling for a rate hike.
"It's not a slam dunk call, but there is probably enough supporting evidence for a hike," he wrote in a research note on Monday.
Macquarie Group economist David Doyle agrees. He predicts the Bank of Canada will raise its policy rate by 125 basis points by the end of 2027.
"Our baseline case remains for a rate hike at this month's meeting," he wrote in a note to clients on Monday. "We continue to see a steady rate hike cycle ahead."

items: Deloitte Canada cuts GDP growth forecast by 20% as tariffs grip economy amid Trump's trade war
No Canada-U.S. trade deal expected before American midterm elections: sources

blocks.text: Leah Zlatkin, a licensed mortgage broker and an expert commentator with LowestRates.ca, agrees.
"If there is a hike, I do think it's gonna be a cycle," Zlatkin said.
She points to a recent price drop in the notoriously expensive Greater Toronto Area as a sign that now is a "good time to buy."
"There's a possibility [that] housing prices are going to continue falling, but the reality is, if you'll qualify for the property today, then you'll qualify again later on if rates rise."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Jeff Lagerquist is a senior writer with CBC News based in Toronto. Originally from Erin, Ont., he studied journalism at Toronto Metropolitan University. Jeff previously worked as a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance Canada. He was also a reporter and digital producer for CTV National News, BNN Bloomberg and The Financial Post. In 2025, he was a Columbia University energy journalism fellow.

blocks.text: Republicans push back on Donald Trump’s wavering support for Ukraine
Ariana Baio

Overnight, a handful of Republicans have spoken out against Donald Trump’s softening stance on Russia, threatening to pull financial support for his agenda over his “embarrassing” handling of the Ukraine war.

blocks.caption: President Donald Trump is reflected in protective glass after speaking at a campaign rally at Pitt–Greenville Airport. Photograph: Matt Ramey/AP

blocks.text: Don Bacon, an outgoing congressman in Nebraska, condemned Trump’s actions – which include a stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel and the pausing of sanctions on Moscow – as “absolutely disgraceful” and accused the US president of cozying up to a “war criminal” in Vladimir Putin, his Russian counterpart.
“It really is disgraceful, and the Republicans that I associate with, there’s a lot of us, can’t stand it,” Bacon told CNN on Monday. “I think the president’s leverage in this Congress is shot.”

Last week, Trump waived sanctions imposed on Russia through a law named after his longtime ally and late senator Lindsey Graham. The legislation, which he signed only last month, was intended to increase financial pressure on Russia, more than four years after it invaded Ukraine.

Instead, Trump announced he had struck a deal with Putin to import diesel fuel, which has become more expensive for Americans largely due to Trump’s war with Iran. Trump has previously blamed Ukraine’s strikes on Russia.

articles.title: Australian MP loses both legs after alleged car attack, husband says
articles.summary: Her alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, faces multiple charges and appeared in court for the first time on Wednesday.

blocks.text: Helen Haines, the Australian MP who was hit by a car in what authorities say was a deliberate attack, has lost both her legs, her husband has confirmed.
Phil Haines said the"horrendous incident" caused his wife significant injuries but "her heart and her mind are in good shape". He added that the "good news in all this is that she's alive".
The alleged attacker, 43-year-old Brendan Nugent, faces multiple charges and appeared in court for the first time on Wednesday.

Nugent was arrested moments after he allegedly drove his Toyota LandCruiser into the independent MP outside her electorate office in the regional town of Wangaratta, about 240km (150miles) northeast of Melbourne.
Haines' "road to recovery will be long and difficult, but we know she is a fighter," her husband said at a press conference in Melbourne where she is being treated.
"She is a determined person who will do her best, with our support and love, to recover. And that is what we hope for."

He thanked hospital staff and people, both in Australia and internationally, who have shown their concern for Haines, and urged those who want to show their support to donate to the Save the Children fund.
"Please keep sending Helen your love," he added.

Earlier on Wednesday, Nugent appeared at the local court to face three charges: dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury, and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official. Police said more charges may be laid, including attempted murder.
Nugent - a local from the nearby town of Tarrawingee and known as an environmental campaigner - remained silent and emotionless during his brief court appearance.
He did not apply for bail and is due back in court in February. Court documents show he was also charged with cultivating and possessing cannabis.
In court, Nugent's lawyer said that his client had "mental health concerns" but did not give any further detail.
The court also heard that Nugent has a rare neurological condition - idiopathic transverse myelitis - caused by inflammation of the spinal cord.
Victoria Police said its investigation, with support from the Australian Federal Police (AFP), remains ongoing and a motive is yet to be established.
"His motivation for this - what we allege is a deliberate attack - is very much a centrepiece of the investigation," said Victoria Police Commissioner Mike Bush.
"Our people will continue to explore every element, angle and avenue to work that out. It's something that, when we work towards it, discover it, we will present in court."
Nugent was not on the radar of police and there was no intelligence of any threat to Haines before the incident, police said.
Investigators are also looking into whether drug use or medication played a part in the incident and if there was any personal connection between Nugent and Haines.

Nugent's family earlier put out a statement saying they were long-time friends with Haines, who is the independent MP for the regional seat of Indi in Victoria. They described the apparent attack as "devastating and unfathomable".
The incident occurred on Monday afternoon at around 15.35, local time. Moments after the car hit Haines, bystanders pulled Nugent out of the vehicle and detained him.
Jacob and Jackie Evans were among the first on the scene, and said Haines was grateful to them for coming to her aid as she lay severely injured.
"Thank you, you lovely people," is what Haines said to them, according to the Herald Sun.
"She was thanking us, it was incredible," Jackie told Nine's Today programme.
Jacob used a tourniquet he had in a medical kit in his car to help stem the bleeding from one of Haines's legs.
Haines underwent surgery after the incident and lost one of her legs. As of Wednesday morning she has also lost the other leg, her husband Phil told reporters.
The community in Wangaratta, as well as the wider political community, are in shock over the incident in a country where political violence is rare.
Leaders from across the political spectrum have paid tribute to Haines, who was first elected in 2019 and is well regarded by her peers.
Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said he had spoken to Haines's husband several times since the incident.
In an interview with the national broadcaster ABC, Albanese said threats to female politicians were marked by a "different form of vilification and aggression" such as threats of rape.
There has also been a recent growing trend of threats against "high office holders", with almost one person a week being charged for such offences, police said.
Monday's incident has sparked debate over the level of security for MPs.
Federal police said that individual protection for every one of the country's 226 federal MPs would require "incredible" levels of staffing.
Instead, police assess the need for close personal protection based on a person's role and the threat environment around them, police said.
Australia's Governor-General Sam Mostyn, who spoke at the same press conference as Haines' husband, said this was "a moment for us to pause, and to choose to be better".
"We should do what I imagine Helen would be doing if she was not the victim of this terrible attack - reaching out to those who are terribly distressed by what has happened," she says.
"Most importantly, that we learn or re-learn to exercise our muscle of decency."

articles.title: Palace on Atong Ang escape: Investigation needed to find lapses
articles.summary: Malacañang on Wednesday said there's a need to investigate to find out the lapses that led to the escape from the country of businessman Atong Ang, who is facing charges in connection with the…

blocks.text: Published October 21, 2026 3:49pm

Malacañang on Wednesday said there's a need to investigate to find out the lapses that led to the escape from the country of businessman Atong Ang, who is facing charges in connection with the alleged killing and disappearance of cockfighting enthusiasts, the so-called missing sabungeros.

Ang is suspected to be the mastermind behind the abduction of the missing sabungeros, and despite being a high-profile figure, he managed to flee the country, according to the Department of the Interior and Local Government.

“Tingnan po natin at sa ngayon ay dapat malaman natin, maimbestigahan kung talagang may lapses. So, may mga tao talaga na mabibilis tumakbo at hindi naman ito ang unang pagkakataon na tumakas itong si Atong Ang – noong unang nakasuhan din ito, nakaalpas din ito agad-agad,” Castro said in a media briefing when asked who was responsible for letting Ang get away.

(We will have to see and determine, to investigate if there really are lapses. There really are some people who are fast to run, after all this is not the first time that Ang escaped — when he first faced a case, he was able to get away fast.)
Castro also said that it was not certain when Ang escaped, as he could have gone out of the country before he was issued an arrest warrant.

“Kung ikaw ay tumalilis na at nagpunta sa ibang bansa ay hindi natin masisi ang gobyerno dahil karapatan ng bawat sinuman kung wala pang warrant of arrest at wala pang hold departure order na nai-issue ang korte,” Castro said.

(If you leave and go to another country then the government could not be blamed because everyone has the right to leave if they do not have an arrest warrant and there is no hold departure order issued by the court.)
Asked if Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla still enjoyed President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. 's trust, Castro said that it would appear so.
“Sa ngayon wala tayong masasabing hindi. Kasi kung wala, masasabi ko na sa inyo,” Castro said. (For now, we cannot say no. Because if there is none, we will tell you about it.)
Ang was issued an arrest warrant in January, in connection with kidnapping and homicide.

Aside from reporting that Ang got away, Remulla also admitted regretting that he was unable to arrest Senator Ronaldo “Bato” Dela Rosa, who is wanted by the International Criminal Court for crimes against humanity.
Pressed on whether there were no perceived lapses with the string of escaped personalities, Castro said that those who needed to be caught should be caught.

articles.summary: PHP is used across large parts of the internet, and speculation has circulated over the past day that websites running the software could be exposed to serious cyber intrusions

items: PHP developers announced patches for two critical vulnerabilities rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 scale, urging users to upgrade immediately.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

The developers of the widely used PHP programming language said on Wednesday, October 21, they would release patches for two critical vulnerabilities, as EU cybersecurity officials warned organizations unable to apply the fixes should take affected websites offline.
PHP is used across large parts of the internet, and speculation has circulated over the past day that websites running the software could be exposed to serious cyber intrusions.

“PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn’t even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood,” cybersecurity company Huntress said in a blog post.
In a security update, PHP said both vulnerabilities were rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale and urged users to “upgrade as soon as the release is available”.
It said a patch for both vulnerabilities was scheduled for 1400 GMT on Wednesday.

The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said on Tuesday in an advisory that the 9.2 rating indicated a risk of unauthenticated remote code execution, a type of flaw that can allow attackers to run malicious code on vulnerable systems without logging in.
CERT-EU urged organisations to prepare for the immediate patching of affected assets and said those unable to do so should consider taking affected sites offline.

The Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) issued similar guidance, urging organisations to identify PHP systems in their environments, prepare to apply patches and monitor applications for signs of malicious activity.
“ACSC is currently not aware of active exploitation related to these vulnerabilities,” the agency said.

Web hosting provider GoDaddy said the flaws could allow attackers to execute code on affected servers over the internet, potentially leading to data theft, website defacement or full system compromise.
PHP’s security team said details of the vulnerabilities, affected versions and the fixed releases would be published when patches are issued.
CERT-EU and the ACSC said all PHP versions from PHP 5 onward could be affected, although PHP has not disclosed which versions are vulnerable. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Labour accused of ‘climate vandalism’ by Green leader Polanski after Jackdaw gasfield approved – UK politics live
articles.summary:
The Jackdaw field will start supplying gas to homes and businesses from the end of the month, the government said

Good morning. After months of delay, the government has taken a decision on…

blocks.text: Good morning. After months of delay, the government has taken a decision on one of the most difficult climate crisis/energy supply challenges on the table. It has approved the Jackdaw gasfield, east of Aberdeen. Peter Walker and Kiran Stacey have the story here.
Here is the government’s news release. And if you want to all the technical documents relating to the decision, you will find them here.

At the last election, Labour said it would not approve new oil and gas licences for the North Sea, but that it would allow existing projects to go ahead. But two projects that had been approved by the Tories – Jackdaw, and the Rosebank oilfield – were blocked by the courts who ordered a rethink, and Labour decided to treat them as existing projects, not brand new ones. But that did not mean Jackdaw and Rosebank were automatically going to be approved.

Over the past 12 months or so, largely as a result of high global energy prices, the public and political debate has shifted, and pressure to allow more ongoing North Sea extraction got stronger. Today’s decision did not come as a surprise. But the Rosebank decision will be a much tougher one because its carbon emissions are far higher than Jackdaw’s, and the environmental argument against it is stronger.
In a statement, Andy Burnham described today’s decision as an example of the “pragmatic approach” he wants to take to energy policy. He said:

double quotation markI welcome the energy secretary’s decision, which will protect hundreds of jobs and help keep millions of homes warm this winter. At a time when people are really struggling, it’s right that we look in a responsible way at maximising the existing energy reserves we have in Britain that could help. We’re committed to moving towards renewable energy and reaching net zero by 2050. But even on our ambitious climate path, we’ll still require oil and gas as part of our energy needs for decades to come. That’s why we’re taking a pragmatic approach to the North Sea. We’re also establishing a new Energy Wealth Fund to invest in renewable energy, support the green transition and help reduce energy bills over the long-term.

Some Labour figures are alarmed at the decision, but so far there has been very little public criticism of the move from the party’s MPs. The other main parties support Jackdaw going ahead. But the Greens have denounced the decision very strongly. This is from their leader, Zack Polanski.

double quotation markThis is climate vandalism. Today’s decision by Labour is a betrayal of all of our futures, Labour has abandoned all credibility in the fight against climate change. The energy secretary has herself said it will make no difference to energy bills; the health secretary has admitted the summer heatwave added to pressure on the NHS, and the industry’s own assessment is that it will create only 27 jobs. This is a victory for Shell over the people.
Here is the agenda for the day.
Morning: Douglas Alexander, the Scottish secretary, is on a visit to a gas terminal in Peterhead to promote the Jackdaw decision.
Noon: Andy Burnham faces Kemi Badenoch at PMQs.
After 12.30pm: Miatta Fahnbulleh, the energy secretary, is expected to make a statement to MPs about the Jackdaw decision.
2.10pm: Michelle O’Neill, Northern Ireland’s first minister, and Emma Little-Pengelly, the deputy first minister, give evidence to Stormont’s executive office committee.
Afternoon: Burnham welcomes Haitham bin Tariq, the Sultan of Oman, to Downing Street.

articles.title: Fact check: Hev Abi didn't curse at Marcos over bucket advice
articles.summary: Viral graphic falsely attributes profane remark to Hev Abi over Marcos’ bucket advice.

blocks.text: October 21, 2026 | 3:34pm
Filipino rapper Hev Abi and President Bongbong Marcos.

MANILA, Philippines — A viral Facebook graphic falsely attributes to Filipino rapper Hev Abi a profane remark directed at President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. over his advice to buy buckets to collect rainwater ahead of El Niño.
In an October 17 Facebook post, the graphic attributed to Hev Abi a vulgar statement, saying he would make Marcos “suck” the rainwater he collected.
Facebook posts falsely attributed a profane remark against President Bongbong Marcos to rapper Hev Abi.
Screenshot taken Oct. 21, 2026, 3 p.m.
The quote in the graphic said:
Bongbong Marcos yung maiipon kong tubig ulan ipapahigop ko sayong taratando ka.
The graphic, posted by Facebook page State News Online, was accompanied by a caption supposedly contextualizing the rapper’s statement.
Part of the post’s caption read:

HEV ABI FIRES BACK AT THE PRESIDENT OVER BUCKET ADVICE Filipino rapper Hev Abi took a swipe at President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. over the latter’s advice for Filipinos to prepare for the anticipated El Niño phenomenon, including the suggestion to buy buckets to store water in preparation for possible shortages.
Another Facebook account, Moto Zinio, shared a purported screenshot of the rapper’s post showing a red-background profile picture and the name “Hev Abi,” but no verification badge.
Rating: This is false.
Facts
Hev Abi did not release any such statement on his official Facebook page, and the alleged quote from the rapper was debunked by his record label.
Urban Department PH debunked the viral graphic attributed to Hev Abi as “fake” in an October 19 statement.
Independent music label Urban Department PH flagged the graphic featuring Hev Abi’s supposed insults against Marcos as “fake” in a statement on October 19.
A graphic accompanying the label’s statement includes a screenshot of State News Online’s post with a “FAKE” stamp on top.

In its post, Urban Department PH also said any other accounts or statements found outside of the rapper’s official page “are not affiliated with nor endorsed by the artist,” and encouraged the public to be “vigilant” in engaging with or sharing content from “fake” or “illicit” accounts.
The label’s statement was shared on Hev Abi’s official Facebook page.
Meanwhile, the purported screenshot of Hev Abi’s post lacks the check mark or verified badge displayed on his official page.
Why we fact-checked this
Marcos drew ire on October 11 after advising the public to buy buckets to collect rainwater in preparation for possible water shortages ahead of the expected El Niño.
Palace Press Officer Claire Castro defended the president's remarks and urged the public to take Marcos' advice seriously for El Niño preparations.

“Sineseryoso ng pangulo ang magaganap at nagaganap na at maaaring mag-worsen sa mga susunod na buwan. Ang bawat pagtalakay dito, ang bawat mensahe, ang bawat suggestion, ang bawat mga binibigay na aral sa atin ng gobyerno at ng pangulo, ito ay dapat na sineseryoso,” Castro said at an October 13 press briefing.

As of October 21, State News Online’s post has garnered more than 77,000 reactions, 20,000 comments and 3,000 shares. Meanwhile, Moto Zinio’s post has obtained at least 5,000 reactions, 300 comments and 200 shares.

articles.title: #ScamAlert chat room launched as digital and financial scams evolve
articles.summary: The new chat room helps users flag scams, learn digital safety tips, and foster community vigilance

items: Iza Estinopo shared her mother's near-victimization by a scam involving a hacked Facebook account, highlighting the importance of awareness and vigilance against digital scams.
The #ScamAlert Laguna forum gathered nearly 200 participants to discuss rising digital scams and introduced a chat room for community members to report scams and share resources.
Experts emphasized the evolving nature of scams, including the use of AI and the recruitment of money mules, while providing strategies for individuals to protect themselves from becoming victims.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

LAGUNA, Philippines – Iza Estinopo, a local resident of San Pedro, recalled a 5 am call from her mother, a senior citizen. Her mother said a friend had sent P3,000 and immediately got P25,000 back. She was sure it was real because she had been chatting with that friend on Facebook.
Her mother pressed Estinopo to send funds through GCash, which Estinopo did not have in her account. An hour later, her mother called again. The friend’s Facebook account had been hacked.
“Buti na lang napigilan siya at saka hindi pa siya marunong mag-GCash that time,” Estinopo said.
(Good thing we stopped her, and she didn’t know how to use GCash yet back then.)

Stories like hers took center stage on Monday, October 19, at #ScamAlert Laguna, a forum that drew nearly 200 people, from senior citizens and students to barangay workers, to the Pacita Astrodome in San Pedro. The event called attention to a rise in digital and financial scams, and gave attendees tactics and resources to stay vigilant and protected.
The afternoon was hallmarked by attendees joining and engaging in Rappler’s new chat room, #ScamAlert, housed in Muni, a community-building platform found on Rappler’s free app.
During the forum, participants and organizers used the chat room to swap personal scam stories, takeaways and resources to become scam-proof.

blocks.caption: LAUNCH. Rappler’s head of civiv engagement Jene Pangue introduced “ScamAlert Chat Room”on Muni in San Pedro City, Laguna on October 19, 2026. The launch is supported by DILG Laguna, the City Government of San Pedro and SmartCT as the platform enables community members to report scams and receive…

blocks.text: Although the chat room was initially launched on-ground in San Pedro, Laguna, the space allows users to connect directly with authorities and fact-checkers, sharing screenshots to verify scam threats or learn about scammers’ latest methods to enforce community vigilance. It can be used by other individuals and groups in other areas as well.

The afternoon brought together partners across sectors to raise awareness around digital safety. Rappler’s civic engagement arm MovePH joined SmartCT, the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Laguna, and the City Government of San Pedro in organizing the event.

The convening was also part of Scam Ready ASEAN, a regional program implemented by the ASEAN Foundation with support from Google.org to build resilience and awareness among communities against online scams and fraud.

It also builds on MovePH’s ongoing #ScamAlert campaign launched in 2025, which has brought digital safety and scam prevention roadshows to various communities across the Philippines, including previous stops in Laguna and Manila.
“Events like this serve as the starting point for bringing together these types of stakeholders,” said Jay Beltran, Laguna Provincial Director of DILG.

blocks.caption: AUDIENCE. Participants download and play SmartCT’s ‘Be Scam Ready’ gameplay experience, which walks through real-life digital scams citizens may face today. Photo by Jake Gomez/Rappler.

blocks.text: When SmartCT executive director Kris Libunao asked the room whether anyone had been scammed, dozens of attendees raised their hands.
Stories like Estinopo’s are why Libunao warns that no one is immune.

“Even if you are a tech person, even if you are an educated person, you can still be scammed dahil hindi ito naaayon sa inyong kaalaman, but sa emotions niyo,” Libunao said. (Even if you are a tech person, even if you are an educated person, you can still be scammed because it doesn’t depend on your knowledge, but on your emotions.)

Gemma Mendoza, Rappler’s head of strategic programs, walked attendees through how integrated the internet is in Filipinos’ daily lives, and how the current-day digital landscape allows scams to thrive.

“Hindi lang important na masaya tayo sa digital. Napaka-importante na maingat din tayo sa digital,” she said. (It’s not enough that we enjoy being online. It’s very important that we’re also careful online.)

During her presentation, Mendoza showed a deepfake video of Rappler CEO Maria Ressa spreading fraudulent claims about cures for diabetes, then broke down the digital forensics of the video. While her mouth, which did not match her speech, gave away the doctored video – the voice actually sounded like Ressa’s.

Digital scams, from phishing attempts to identity fraud, are already a mainstay of modern life, but artificial intelligence tools, like voice cloning, are rapidly scaling the number of scams, and the variety.
“Hindi lang nagbibigay ng impormasyon ang AI sa atin kundi, kumukuha rin ito ng impormasyon sa atin,” Mendoza said. “Kailangan maging maingat tayo sa pagshare ng impormasyon online.”
(“AI doesn’t just provide us with information, it also collects information from us,” Mendoza said. “We need to be careful when sharing information online.”)

blocks.caption: CONTEXT. Rappler’s head of strategic programs Gemma Mendoza walks attendees through today’s modern scam landscape, and AI’s role in creating and spreading false information. Photo by Jake Gomez/Rappler

blocks.text: But some threats seek to make everyday Filipinos complicit in crimes, warned lawyer Marco Mendoza of the Consumer Account Protection Office under the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP).
Scammers are now recruiting money mules – people who let criminals use their bank or e-wallet accounts to receive and move illicit funds – often for as little as P400 to P500, he said.

“Ang nagiging ano kasi nila approach nila ngayon is nag-re-recruit sila on a massive scale…. Tapos ‘yung mga nagbebenta, nagpahiram na ‘yon, hindi nila alam most of the time kung saan gagamitin ‘yung financial accounts nila,” Marco Mendoza said.
(Their approach now is to recruit on a massive scale…. And those who sold or lent [their accounts], most of the time, don’t know where their financial accounts will be used.)

Once a victim’s money lands in a mule account, scammers rarely leave it there. They “layer” the funds, splitting them and moving them across sprawling networks of accounts to make them harder for law enforcement to trace.
Under the Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFSA), acting as a money mule is punishable by law.
Clarence dela Cruz, project officer at SmartCT, led participants through the organization’s Be Scam Ready gameplay, which simulated some of the scams Filipinos may face in their everyday lives.
Testing the audience, Dela Cruz displayed fake texts and emails from claimed legitimate entities like government agencies and banks, breaking down the tell-tale signs of a scam message.
Libunao said the game is backed by behavioral science, and that training that simulates scams is key to understanding and preparing for the real thing.

“In the event of a fire drill, not an actual fire, we go over what we should do during an emergency,” she said. “If you play [the game] from your own perspective, you will actually see how you can become scam-ready.”
Mendoza of the BSP shared with the crowd how Filipinos can protect themselves, especially as consumers.

“Whenever you are conducting financial transactions or managing your financial accounts, take a second or two, pause for a moment… Use those two seconds to consider: what is the right course of action? Should I really click this? Do I need to provide this information, or should I verify it with my bank first?” Mendoza said in a mix of English and Filipino.
He stressed that one-time passwords or PINs (OTPs) and other sensitive personal information should never be shared with anyone.
Scam victims can dial 1326 to reach the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center, where they can report the incident and get assistance.
Individuals and institutions committed in fighting digital fraud can also join the #ScamAlert chat room for free. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: What you need to know

items: Germany's Finance Ministry has erroneously introduced an approved tax hike on tobacco products months before it was scheduled to come into effect
A 'technical error' with incorrect dates is said to have caused the flub
The issue is further complicated by the fact that tax stamps for the new rate are not yet ready, meaning tobacco companies cannot pay the new, significantly higher rate
Alice Weidel of the AfD will pitch what she is calling "A New Deal for Europe" in Strasbourg this afternoon
NVIDIA's Jensen Huang will deliver the keynote address at a Berlin AI conference on AI chips, infrastructure, software and robotics

blocks.text: October 21, 2026
Tobacco tax introduced months early
Germany's Finance Ministry said that a "technical error" had led to the early introduction of a steep tax hike on tobacco products.
The hike received final parliamentary approval on Friday and had been scheduled to go into effect at the turn of the year.
Instead the changes officially gazetted on Tuesday stated that they would come into force on Wednesday.
"A technical error occurred in the documents regarding the effective date," said the Ministry, adding that a correction had been initiated.
The changes are expected to pump some €12 billion ($13.5 billion) in added tax revenue over the next four years.
However, tobacco companies will be unable to pay the higher rate due to the fact that new tax stamps are not yet available.
Currently, a 20-pack of cigarettes costs around €8-€10. The Finance Ministry expects that price to rise to between €12 and €14 per pack.
Roughly 1-in-5 people (19%) smoke in Germany, with around 130,000 dying of tobacco-related illness each year.

Although health experts and politicians hope that higher prices will deter people from smoking, the German Customs Union and the tobacco industry warn that smokers could simply turn to contraband cigarettes instead.
